first.rationale: Prioritize a guarded onboarding-simplification experiment because completion and activation are both declining, and inherited evidence indicates this can improve time-to-value and early adoption. Verify the prior onboarding result and the pricing retention trade-off before committing; do not assume competitor pricing warrants a retention-damaging response.

mid.rationale: Run onboarding simplification. It directly addresses both falling onboarding completion and activation, while the verified prior result showed completion +13%, time-to-value down 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. Do not use promotional pricing this cycle: despite competitor pressure and short-term qualified-revenue lift, its verified -12% 30-day retention and failure to survive the first renewal cycle conflict with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Use a standard experiment with retention and qualified-revenue cohort guardrails rather than assuming prior effects fully reproduce.

final2.rationale: Continue the onboarding-simplification experiment rather than react with deeper promotional pricing. The verified onboarding result improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly addressing current activation and completion declines. The available pricing evidence shows short-term qualified-revenue gains but materially worse retention and failure through the first renewal cycle, which conflicts with the long-term qualified-revenue objective even amid intensified price pressure. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn as a guardrail and reassess next cycle when verification capacity returns.
